name: @adminium/server
description: Fastify server: REST /api/v1, auth, jobs, serves the dashboard build
//engines: The floor is Node-API 10, which better-sqlite3 13's prebuilt binaries need.
Node has it from 22.14, and on the 23 line from 23.6. An older Node does not
throw: it segfaults while loading the driver, and better-sqlite3's own
engines (>=22) lets npm install it without a warning. npm only warns on
engines, so src/cli/index.ts refuses an old Node before loading anything
(src/cli/node-support.ts). Keep the two in step; the pin lives in

scripts.prepack: node scripts/bundle-dashboard.mjs && node scripts/bundle-allowlists.mjs && node scripts/bundle-samples.mjs

//dependencies: `pino-pretty` is a RUNTIME dependency, not a dev one (app.ts buildLogger).
pino loads a transport target by NAME, inside a worker it spawns, so no
static gate sees it: not tsc, not dependency-cruiser, not the bundler. It
shipped as a devDependency through 0.2.5, where the default gate (dev +
a TTY) is ON for every human install — so `npx @adminiumjs/adminium` threw
`unable to determine transport target for "pino-pretty"` the instant the
wizard booted the server, and `adminium start` never started at all. Every
existing buildLogger test passed `pretty: false`, so the suite was blind;
the pin lives in test/m10-regressions.test.ts under `packaging`.
//optionalDependencies: src/meta/store.ts opens the meta store with a bare `await import('pg')` /
`import('mysql2')`. They are declared HERE, on the server, and not merely
specifier resolves against the IMPORTING package's node_modules: the
isolated tree where an adapter's own dependency lands under .pnpm and is
unreachable from /app/dist. Without these the published image can run only
the embedded SQLite fallback the docs tell people not to use in
production, while docker-compose.yml documents a postgres meta store — a
crash-loop under `restart: unless-stopped`, with the printed remedy
(`npm install pg`) impossible inside a non-root image.
OPTIONAL, not required: both are pure JS so they always install in
practice, but `--no-optional` stays a supported way to ship a SQLite-only
install, and MetaDriverMissingError still explains that case.
